program-expectations.title: Program Expectations
program-expectations.html:
To cultivate a community of STEM scholars who will produce sustainable solutions to global challenges and actively engage as thought leaders in society

MSP expects all scholars to:

  • Prioritize social, emotional, mental, and physical well-being
  • Maintain a 3.5 GPA

  • Live out the program’s Pillars of Success: Accountability, Cohesiveness, Academic Excellence, Vision, Character, Respect, and Resilience

  • Complete Summer Bridge
  • Enroll in MSP courses and seminars
  • Meet regularly with the MSP Assistant Program Directors
  • Attend all MSP activities (family meetings, Stress Busters, etc.)
  • Participate in STEM research during the summer and academic year
  • Live in the MSP living and learning community for the first two years
  • Meet the academic requirements of their major departments and the MSP program
  • Give back to their community through participation in community service opportunities
  • Be an active participant in the MSP and Penn State communities
  • Explore student engagement opportunities
  • Delay joining a fraternity or sorority until junior year
  • Complete a senior research thesis or publication
  • Apply to Ph.D. programs

Learn more about general program expectations on the Current Scholars page

featured-scholars-2.title: Featured Scholars
featured-scholars-2.html:
DISCOVERY. LEADERSHIP. IMPACT.

Scholars making their mark.

Meet Millennium Scholars whose research, presentations, and achievements have been recognized by Penn State and national organizations.

Recent scholar stories

The latest features and program updates, followed by earlier stories below.

RESEARCH PRESENTATION · APRIL 2026

Kaelonnah Darlich

Monarch research on a national stage

Millennium Scholar Kaelonnah Darlich presented at the National Conference on Undergraduate Research in Richmond, Virginia, in April 2026.

  • Her entomology research examines how simulated heat waves affect monarch butterfly development, reproduction, and mate selection.
  • She conducts this work with arthropod ecologist Mônica Kersch-Becker.
  • She also received a 2026 Stand Up Award for Undergraduate Ethical Leadership.
Read the full story Read about the Stand Up Award

GOLDWATER SCHOLARSHIP · 2026–27

Kieran Sturges

Computing that advances communication research

Millennium Scholar Kieran Sturges earned a 2026–27 Goldwater Scholarship, recognizing his academic achievement and research experience.

  • His studies combine computer science and mathematics.
  • In Penn State’s Speech, Language and Swallowing study, he develops computational and AI-based methods to improve research procedures.
  • His research interests connect computing with communication sciences and disorders, including speech and swallowing outcomes in individuals with Down syndrome.
Read the full story

TEDxPSU · FEBRUARY 7, 2026

Scholar voices at TEDxPSU 2026

Public engagement and event leadership

Sofia spoke about the importance of ethical research in Indigenous communities at TEDxPSU 2026. Kieran and Marisa helped organize the event, bringing scholar perspectives to both the stage and the planning team.

  • Sofia spoke about ethical research in Indigenous communities.
  • Kieran and Marisa helped organize TEDxPSU 2026.
Read the full story

MORE DISCOVERY. MORE IMPACT.

More scholar stories

Earlier research, achievements, and scholar experiences, from newest to oldest.

ABRCMS · NOVEMBER 22, 2025

Five scholars recognized at ABRCMS

Research presentations earning recognition

Amirah, Isley, Giselle, Isaiah, and Kaelonnah received recognition for their research presentations at ABRCMS 2025.

  • Five Millennium Scholars earned recognition for sharing their research at a national conference.
  • Their recognition was for research presentations at ABRCMS 2025.
Read the full story

RESEARCH AND MENTORING · SEPTEMBER 24, 2025

Matias Moreno

Energy research and peer mentoring

Materials science and engineering scholar Matias Moreno researched fuel cell catalyst layers at Berkeley Lab during summer 2025. As an Undergraduate Research Ambassador, he helps students find research mentors, develop posters, and apply for REU opportunities.

  • He studied fuel cell catalyst layers at Berkeley Lab during summer 2025.
  • As an Undergraduate Research Ambassador, he supports students with mentors, posters, and REU applications.
Read the full story

ALUMNI ACHIEVEMENT · 2025

Bridget Reheard

Environmental research and a national fellowship

Millennium Scholar Bridget Reheard was named the College of Earth and Mineral Sciences’ summer 2025 student marshal and received a 2025 National Science Foundation Graduate Research Fellowship.

  • She graduated summa cum laude with a 4.0 GPA and degrees in geosciences and wildlife and fisheries science.
  • Her undergraduate research examined shale gas development and aquatic communities, alongside summer projects involving environmental contaminants.
  • She planned to begin doctoral study in Integrated Toxicology and Environmental Health at Duke University in fall 2025.
Read the full story

MIT SUMMER RESEARCH · AUGUST 7, 2025

David and Valeria

Summer research presentations at MIT

David (Cohort 10) and Valeria (Cohort 9) participated in the MIT Summer Research Program and presented their research in August 2025.

  • David is a member of Cohort 10; Valeria is a member of Cohort 9.
  • Both participated in the MIT Summer Research Program and presented their work in August 2025.
Read the full story

NASA BIG IDEA CHALLENGE · 2020

Lia Formica

Designing instruments for lunar discovery

Lia Formica, a Cohort 7 scholar studying aerospace engineering, worked with Penn State’s Student Space Programs Lab on the 2020 NASA Big Idea Challenge.

  • Her structures team helped design an instrument for light-induced breakdown spectroscopy in a permanently shadowed region of the Moon.
  • The project explored the use of a laser to identify elements and compounds in lunar regolith.
  • In her original profile, Lia also described her Air Force ROTC training and her interest in future research on space systems and defense capabilities.

Lia is from Whitehouse Station, New Jersey. Her original profile described her as a junior in aerospace engineering and a member of Cohort 7. The spectroscopy project explored lunar elements and compounds, including water.

Her Air Force ROTC experience included weekly physical training, leadership laboratory meetings, and air class, preparing cadets to commission as second lieutenants. Outside her studies, she enjoyed spending time with her siblings, reading, and flying lessons at Bellefonte Airport. She hoped to serve in the Air Force and conduct research on space system structures or military defense capabilities.

This feature describes Lia’s experience at the time of the 2020 project.

Millennium Scholars receive financial, academic, and advising support. They study collaboratively, conduct research, and maintain strong academic records as they work toward doctoral study in STEM.

The parents of Millennium Scholars are vital to the program’s success.

The Millennium Scholars Parent Association enables parents to engage with each other and support the program. The Association assists the program with Interview Weekend, Summer Bridge welcome events, and various activities throughout the academic year.

We expect and encourage parent engagement from Interview Weekend until graduation. Once your student completes Summer Bridge, you will be invited to participate in the Millennium Scholars Parent Association.

If you are a parent of an MSP scholar and would like to be part of the Millennium Scholars Parent Association, please contact us at millennium@psu.edu

faculty-mentors.title: Faculty Mentors
faculty-mentors.html:
Faculty mentors are an important part of the Millennium Scholars Program. They help scholars develop laboratory skills, cultivate research interests, and find opportunities to conduct research.

Serving as a faculty mentor benefits the mentors and students. The opportunity to connect and collaborate with students is often personally and professionally rewarding.

The Millennium Scholars Program welcomes faculty who are interested in mentoring in formal and informal ways, such as offering students the opportunity to conduct laboratory research. Faculty mentors are also encouraged to talk about graduate school preparation. If you are interested in becoming a faculty mentor, please contact millennium@psu.edu

Many Penn State faculty members mentor Millennium Scholars in their studies and related lab work. This is a critical component of the Millennium Scholars Program, through which participating students have ample opportunities to prepare for future graduate study in STEM fields.

senior-thesis.title: Senior Thesis
senior-thesis.html:
The thesis is the culmination of each Millennium Scholar’s research experience. Writing a research thesis gives each scholar the opportunity to demonstrate research abilities and proficiency in a STEM-related topic.

By conducting research and writing the thesis under the supervision of faculty mentors, scholars strengthen faculty relationships, deepen their understanding of a topic, and contribute to expanding the frontiers of knowledge in their fields. The process also enables scholars to enhance their research and communication skills, which are critical to success in graduate studies and future careers.

A Millennium Scholar’s thesis must be based on STEM-related research in which the student has participated, as guided by a faculty supervisor in a department of one of the five colleges affiliated with the Millennium Scholars Program.

The thesis should follow the format of a scientific paper in the scholar’s discipline, with an introduction; methods, results, and discussion sections; and appropriate acknowledgments and references.

MSP Thesis Template Request the MSP thesis signatory page Thesis Submission Site

YOUR RESEARCH ROADMAP

Your thesis, step by step.

Start your research as early as possible, ideally in your first year. These milestones show the latest point at which each step should be completed.

Faculty approval date

The source content lists April 16, 2021. Contact the MSP team for the faculty approval deadline for your graduating class.

Set monthly goals with your supervisor for background reading, data collection, and thesis drafts. Schedule regular meetings to monitor and discuss your progress.

Thesis Submission Requirements

The completion of the thesis submission process culminates in the electronic submission of the thesis to the Millennium Scholars Thesis Website. The official copy of the thesis will be on file with the University Libraries.

All submissions should be made in PDF format. To graduate as a Millennium Scholar, students need to meet all submission deadlines.

All Millennium Scholars need to submit a thesis to the Millennium Scholars Website. If you are a member of the Schreyer Honors College, you will submit your thesis to both websites.

Format Review (submission deadline: February 1 of senior year)

  1. Submit a single PDF of the draft of your thesis. This draft will be reviewed to ensure scholars are following formatting guidelines. The thesis does not have to be complete for this submission, but the draft should contain all of the sections that will appear in the final thesis.

  2. The name of the file should be LastName_FirstName_ThesisTitle.pdf (e.g., Green_Joy_DevCElegans.pdf).
  3. Submit your draft for format review at the Millennium Scholars Thesis website.
Final Submission (submission deadline: approximately April 10 of senior year)
  1. Carefully proofread the thesis, including the title and signatory pages.
  2. Add your academic vita at the end of your thesis.
  3. Save the final thesis in PDF format.

  4. Complete the signatory page. The signatory page is not submitted electronically. Collect the signatures and submit the signatory page to the Millennium Scholars Program office. Make sure the names and titles on the signatory page are exactly the same as those on the title page of your thesis. Students who are also in the Schreyer Honors College may submit a copy of the signatory page.

Go to the Millennium Scholars Thesis website and upload your final thesis.
Final Approval

The author and thesis supervisor will be notified when the final thesis is approved. Your thesis will be publicly available within a month after graduation unless you have requested restricted access.

Thesis Templates

Please use the formatting guidelines and thesis templates provided in the links to the right. Members of the Schreyer Honors College should use the template and guidelines provided here. If your department has a specific template or formatting guidelines, please use the template and guidelines provided by your department. Keep in mind that your thesis should follow the formatting and style of professional writing in your discipline. Consult with your thesis supervisor to ensure that your style and formatting are appropriate for your discipline.

Fonts and Color

Font type: Times New Roman.

Font size: Use 11- or 12-point type. Smaller type is permitted in tables, figures, and appendices.

Font color: The text of the thesis should be black. Color is permitted in figures, tables, charts, etc.

Organization and Page Numbers

Organization: Each section of the thesis should begin on a new page. This includes elements of the front matter (abstract, acknowledgments, etc.), the reference sections, and appendices.

Do not type a heading near the bottom of a page unless there is room for at least two lines of text after the heading.

Page Numbers: All pages in the thesis should be numbered except the title and signatory pages. Pages with figures and tables should be numbered. Lowercase Roman numerals are used for the front matter and Arabic numbers for the text. Please refer to the template regarding page numbers.

Title and Signatory Pages

Title Page: Use the template provided. Please make sure you list the correct professional titles of your thesis supervisor and reviewer. Check with your thesis supervisor or their department for the correct information. Do not include titles such as Dr. or PhD.

Examples: Penny Stater, Associate Professor of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology, Thesis Supervisor; Millie Scholar, Professor of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology, Reviewer

Signatory Page: The signatures on the signatory page indicate that your thesis supervisor and reviewer have approved your final thesis. Each thesis requires at least two signatures: one from your thesis supervisor and one from a reviewer. If your department does not provide a reviewer for your thesis, the Millennium Scholars Program will identify a reviewer for you.

The signatory page should not be included with your electronic submission. Please submit a hard copy to the Millennium Scholars Program office. If you are a member of the Schreyer Honors College, you may submit a copy of your signatory page to the MSP office.

Abstract

The abstract is a brief summary of the content of your thesis. The abstract should be at least one paragraph long but usually no longer than one page. The abstract should motivate the reader to examine the entire thesis. Consider including the following sections in your abstract:

Motivation: Why did you examine this topic?

Problem Statement: What question or questions are you addressing? What problem are you trying to solve?

Methods: What methods did you use to address the question(s)?

Results: What were your findings?

Conclusions: What are the implications of your research? What might the next steps be for this topic or question?


Table of Contents

The table of contents lists the topics of the thesis. You should build your table of contents using the headings in your thesis. The headings in your text should exactly match the headings in the table of contents. The title of each appendix should be included in the table of contents.

Thesis Template, MSP Signatory Page, & Submission Site

Millennium Scholars Thesis Template

Request the MSP thesis signatory page

MSP Thesis Submission Site

Thesis Formatting

Thesis formats should follow specific department and college guidelines as appropriate. Scholars who are also in the Schreyer Honors College (SHC) may use one STEM research-based thesis to meet the thesis requirements of both programs and should follow the SHC thesis guidelines. Links to guidelines provided by the STEM colleges and the SHC are provided in the "Additional Resources" section on this page.

Acknowledgments

Acknowledgments are optional. However, if you would like to thank individuals for providing assistance or support, you may add an acknowledgments section to your thesis. If you received a grant to support your research, you should recognize the grant provider in the acknowledgments. You are strongly encouraged to include an acknowledgments section to thank the people who supported you in this effort.

Tables and Figures

When using tables and figures, be sure to insert your tables and figures rather than copying and pasting them. Right-click to label your table or figure appropriately. With this method, your tables and figures will be linked to the lists in the template when you update those lists.

Captions and numbering

Be sure to number and caption each figure and table. Number them consecutively beginning with 1 or by chapter using a decimal system (e.g., 1.1, 1.2, 1.3, 2.1, 2.2, 2.3).

Placement

Ideally, tables and figures are placed immediately after their first mention. You may also elect to group your tables and figures at the end of each chapter. You may use appendices to include tables and figures that are not as central to the thesis. Always refer to the table or figure by its number. Do not use a phrase like ‘the following table shows’ to reference a table or figure.

Citations, Footnotes, Works Cited and Reference Pages

Please use the appropriate style as dictated by your discipline to cite works that you reference in the thesis. Consult with your thesis supervisor regarding the most appropriate style guide for your work. The librarians at Penn State Libraries can also provide assistance regarding proper citation format. You may consider purchasing the appropriate style guide manual. Once the style you will use has been determined, follow the rules closely and consistently. In addition to citing works used within the paper, your thesis must include a bibliography. Again, use the format that is appropriate for your discipline and consistent with the format you used for citing works within the paper.

Appendices

You may have other material that is relevant but not directly referenced in the text of the thesis or is too lengthy or detailed to include in the body of the thesis (raw data, procedural explanations, etc.). This material may be placed in an appendix. Appendices should be designated A, B, C (not 1, 2, 3 or I, II, III). If there is only one appendix, call it simply Appendix, not Appendix A. Titles of appendices must be listed in the table of contents. Appendix pages must be numbered consecutively with the text of the thesis (do not number the pages A-1, A-2, etc.).

Academic Vita

The academic vita is required and must be the last page of the document. Do not give the vita a page number and do not list it in the table of contents. The title – Academic Vita – and the author’s name should appear at the top. A standard outline style or a prose form may be used. This should be structured similarly to a résumé. Do not include your GPA.

faq.title: FAQ
faq.html:
We are excited that you are interested in the Millennium Scholars Program and would like to learn more. If you have any additional questions, feel free to contact us at Millennium@psu.edu

Application Process

Can I apply to the Millennium Scholars Program after I have enrolled at Penn State, or if I am transferring to Penn State from another college or university?

No. Only current high school seniors can apply to the program. Learn more about the application process on our How to Apply page.

Can I start at another Penn State campus (besides University Park) and be a Millennium Scholar?
No. Millennium Scholars candidates must attend classes at the University Park campus for all four years. Scholars begin their studies during the summer between their senior year of high school and their first fall semester at University Park. Learn more about the application process on our How to Apply page.
If I do not receive an offer of admission to the Millennium Scholars Program, can I still participate in some way?
Although only students who have attended the Summer Bridge program can graduate as Millennium Scholars, many of our program activities are open to all students, and interested students are welcome to participate in those events. Learn more about the application process on our How to Apply page.
How much does it cost to apply to the Millennium Scholars Program?

There is no additional application fee to apply to the program. Learn more about the application process on our How to Apply page.

Can I appeal the decision if I am not selected to participate in the Millennium Scholars Program?
No. All admission decisions and offers are final. Learn more about the application process on our How to Apply page. Summer Bridge
Do I have to participate in the Summer Bridge program, or can I begin my studies during the fall semester?
All Millennium Scholars must complete the Summer Bridge program. Learn more about Summer Bridge on our Summer Bridge page.
Can I participate in the Learning Edge Academic Program (LEAP) instead of the Millennium Scholars Program’s Summer Bridge?
No, participation in the Summer Bridge program is required of all Millennium Scholars. Learn more about Summer Bridge on our Summer Bridge page.

Life as a Scholar

Can I study abroad while I am a Millennium Scholar?
Yes! Millennium Scholars are encouraged to take advantage of Penn State’s vast Education Abroad offerings. Students work closely with their advisers to identify appropriate education abroad experiences and to build them into the students’ academic plans.
If I am accepted into the Millennium Scholars Program, is my scholarship guaranteed for four years?
No. Renewal of the Millennium Scholars Program scholarship is contingent upon the student maintaining a high GPA and good standing in the program (including participation in program activities, research, and adherence to individualized action plans for success).
How long will it take to graduate?

Millennium Scholars are expected to graduate within four years.

Does my graduate work have to be done at Penn State?

No. We encourage Millennium Scholars to apply to and accept admission to the best graduate programs in their chosen fields, wherever those are.

how-to-apply.title: How to Apply
how-to-apply.html:
PLAN YOUR APPLICATION

Application countdown

December 1, 2026

—Days—Hours—Minutes—Seconds

Time remaining until the target published in MSP’s official countdown.

The official application page’s countdown points to December 1, 2026, while its detailed checklist still lists the 2025–26 cycle. Confirm your application deadline and exact submission time in MyPennState or with the MSP team.

MSP Virtual Application Workshop

Please join us on November 11, 2026, from 7:00 pm – 8:00 pm EST to learn more about the Millennium Scholars Program. You will meet Millennium Scholars staff and current students. We will give an overview of the Millennium Scholars Program, including program benefits and requirements, student experiences, and the application and selection process. Scan below to register or click here.

Application

  1. Complete an undergraduate application through MyPennState or the Common Application, including a complete and accurate high school academic record. The MSP application is only open to incoming first-year students who are U.S. citizens or permanent residents. The application can only be accessed when you apply to Penn State University Park.
  2. Select University Park as your first-choice starting campus on the general Penn State application.
  3. Select an intended major in one of the participating colleges as your academic interest area on the general Penn State application.
  4. A link to the Millennium Scholars application will appear in your MyPennState account 2–3 days after submitting your Penn State application*. Complete and submit the Millennium Scholars Program application.

*It could take at least 3 days to gain access to the MSP application after you submit your Penn State application. Please plan ahead for access to the MSP application.

Essay Questions

The Millennium Scholars essay responses should be no more than 500 words each.
  1. The world faces many challenges, including food insecurity, access to clean water, climate change, and health care disparities. Tell us your intended major and how you will apply it to address any global challenge.
  2. The Millennium Scholars Program provides a supportive, structured, collaborative learning community. What strengths will you bring to the community? How will you contribute to and benefit from the collaborative environment?
  3. How has resilience played a role in your life, and how do you see it affecting your college career?
  4. Reflect on how your unique background and experiences have influenced your interactions with others and shaped your understanding of collaborative work within STEM.

Recommendations

In the Millennium Scholars Program application, you are required to include the names and contact information of two people who will submit recommendations for you. At least one recommendation must come from a math, science, and/or engineering instructor.

Note as of October 23, 2025: The technical problem affecting recommendation submissions has been resolved. Recommenders may submit materials now. If you submitted on or after October 23, you do not need to resubmit.

Exam Scores

List all math and science (calculus, chemistry, physics, biology) Advanced Placement and/or college courses you have taken. The submission of SAT or ACT scores is optional.

Criteria

The Undergraduate Admissions office will evaluate your credentials for admission to the University, and a Millennium Scholars Selection Committee – consisting of program staff, faculty, and deans from the participating colleges – will review your Millennium Scholars Program application. These decisions are made independently of each other. Students should not wait for their admissions decision to submit their Millennium Scholars Program application, although an offer of admission to University Park eventually will be required for admission to the Millennium Scholars Program.

The MSP application is only open to incoming first-year students, and can only be accessed when you apply to Penn State University Park.

Evaluation

  1. A transcript review to evaluate your academic success and background, particularly in math and science courses
  2. An assessment of the written essays.
  3. Review of the letters of recommendation

Successful Applicants

  1. Are high achievers with strong academic records
  2. Are committed to advancing research and technology.
  3. Are eager collaborative learners and team players
  4. Are prepared to work hard, graduate at the top of their classes, and become leaders in STEM-related fields

Previously published application timeline · 2025–26

MSP’s official page still lists the following dates for the previous application cycle. These are retained for reference; do not use them as deadlines for the current cycle.

  • August 1, 2025: Penn State and Millennium Scholars Program applications become available
  • November 1, 2025: Penn State EARLY ACTION filing deadline (Millennium Scholars candidates are strongly encouraged to apply by this deadline.)
  • November 1, 2025: Schreyer Honors College optional interview deadline
  • December 1, 2025 (11:59 p.m. Eastern): Millennium Scholars Program application deadline (All applications and recommendations must be submitted by this date for the application to be evaluated)
  • February 27 and 28, 2026: Interview Weekend on the University Park campus
  • Mid-March 2026: Offers made to Millennium Scholars candidates
  • May 1, 2026: Penn State offer acceptance deadline
  • June–July 2026 (dates to be announced): Summer Bridge program
  • August 24, 2026: First day of fall classes

Required events

Interview Weekend

After all applications have been evaluated, the top 100 candidates will be invited to come to University Park for the last step in the selection process: Interview Weekend. Students and families are responsible for travel costs to University Park for this two-day event, although a limited number of travel grants may be made in cases of demonstrated financial need.

A separate committee will make final admission offer decisions after the candidates’ interviews. Approximately 30–35 students will then be admitted to the Summer Bridge program in preparation for matriculation to Penn State in the fall.

Summer Bridge

Students who accept an offer of admission to Penn State and the Millennium Scholars Program will then arrive on campus in mid-June for a six-week Summer Bridge program. Exact dates will vary from year to year. Successful candidates will receive detailed instructions with their offers from the program. Completion of Summer Bridge is required to matriculate into the Millennium Scholars Program at Penn State.

The Millennium Scholars Program is open to all high-achieving high school seniors who are interested in becoming leaders in STEM-related fields with the ultimate goal of obtaining a doctoral degree in a STEM field.

about-us-2.title: About Us
about-us-2.html:
ESTABLISHED IN 2013

The Penn State Millennium Scholars Program is designed to ensure that scholars not only graduate from Penn State but also go on to become leaders in their chosen fields.

Millennium Scholars receive academic, professional, social, and financial support to ensure students have all the tools they need to achieve academic excellence and success together. All Millennium Scholars receive merit-based scholarship support. Some students may qualify for additional scholarships.

Summer Bridge

Summer Bridge is an intensive six-week program for all incoming Millennium Scholars, held during the summer before their first year. It is an integral and defining part of the Millennium Scholars Program. Completion of Summer Bridge is required to matriculate into the Millennium Scholars Program at Penn State.

The program covers the costs of tuition, room and board, and a variety of professional development activities during Summer Bridge. During the six-week bridge, scholars: (1) begin their academic careers and build relationships within their cohort, (2) take rigorous foundational courses and seminars in math, professional communication skills, chemistry, and engineering, (3) receive an introduction to research at Penn State, (4) learn important life skills, including time management, problem-solving, and smart study habits, and (5) participate in team-building exercises, community service opportunities, social events, and field trips to national labs, museums, and industrial partners.

Scholarly Community

The Penn State Millennium Scholars are a small, tight community of learners, living and working together in a family-like community.

Studying in groups is strongly and consistently encouraged, with scholars from older cohorts contributing to new students’ success. Millennium Scholars live on campus during their first two years of study, and then may choose to stay on campus or move off campus during the third and fourth years.

Academic & Personal Coaching

In addition to advising through their academic colleges and departments, Millennium Scholars receive personalized attention from an academic and administrative team dedicated to their personal and professional success. Assistant Program Directors help scholars navigate their academic studies and lives at a large research university.

Additionally, Millennium Scholars staff provide resources and support for scholars to participate in study abroad opportunities, attend scientific conferences to present the results of their research, and ultimately enroll in top graduate programs in their chosen fields.

Research

Research experience is critical when preparing for Ph.D. or M.D./Ph.D. programs. Penn State’s world-class faculty offer scholars engaging and interactive learning environments in their research labs.

Scholars are required to participate in Penn State research labs during the academic year as well as summer research opportunities or internships on and off of Penn State's campus. The Millennium Scholars Program provides advice and contacts to help scholars obtain summer internships and opportunities to work in research laboratories on campus during each academic year. Scholars are required to complete a research thesis, which helps prepare them for graduate school and future research.

Scholar Expectations

In order to successfully participate in the MSP and graduate as a Scholar, students must follow all program requirements.

  1. Be intentional about emotional, mental, and physical health
  2. Complete Summer Bridge
  3. Be an active participant in the MSP and Penn State communities
  4. Maintain a 3.5 GPA
  5. Attend all MSP activities (Weekly MSP Seminars, family meetings, check-ins with staff, etc.)
  6. Participate in STEM research during the summer and academic year
  7. Live in the MSP living and learning community for the first two years
  8. Delay joining a fraternity or sorority until the third year
  9. Complete a senior research thesis or publication
  10. Apply to Ph.D. programs

our-mission-vision-pillars.title: Our Mission, Vision & Pillars
our-mission-vision-pillars.html:
To cultivate a community of STEM scholars who will produce sustainable solutions to global challenges and actively engage as thought leaders in society

Mission

The Penn State Millennium Scholars Program supports an ambitious group of undergraduate students striving to succeed in the fields of science, technology, engineering, and math (STEM). Millennium Scholars are high-achieving STEM students who want to be leaders and foster innovation in their fields.

Millennium Scholars receive financial, academic, and advising support, and are expected to work hard and study in a collaborative environment, conduct research, and maintain an excellent academic record, with the ultimate goal of obtaining an advanced degree in a STEM field.

The United States is facing a shortfall of Ph.D.-level scientists and engineers. According to the Bureau of Labor Statistics, between 2012 and 2022, the number of scientists and engineers needed to meet growth and net replacement needs will be 2.3 million. Even more critically, we face a shortage of leaders in the STEM fields.

Vision

Our vision is to support an ambitious group of undergraduate students striving to succeed in the fields of science, technology, engineering, and math (STEM). In addition, we endeavor to fill the talent gap in STEM by drawing from our entire population. We must provide more opportunities, role models, inspiration, and financial resources.

Cohesiveness

Character

Vision

Resilience

Why give?

Penn State and its STEM colleges have made a significant financial commitment to the program, but investment from corporate partners will allow us to strengthen and grow the program in the years to come. Private gifts will allow us to provide extraordinary financial support to Millennium Scholars, to enhance the educational features that make this program so unique, and to ensure that the program can continue to flourish for years to come. We are most in need of direct student support, travel awards, and programmatic support.

Ways to Support

Private Donors

Philanthropy will help us to create a supportive, challenging, and academically rich environment for these future leaders, one which will promote their long-term success and enrich the entire campus community. A gift to the Millennium Scholars Program is an investment in our students’ futures, and it is also an investment in the future of Penn State and our nation. Please join us in changing the future of STEM by partnering with us through the Millennium Scholars Program.

Corporate Partners

Corporate partners will help champion our efforts to build a pipeline of STEM researchers and leaders who are committed to advancing science and technology and keeping the United States competitive in the STEM fields. Corporate partnerships reflect the value we place on collaboration with companies that share our commitment to developing the next generation of STEM leaders.

Alumni

The Millennium Scholars Program has graduated eight cohorts of scholars. If you are a Penn State graduate who wants to encourage the achievement of students in STEM, we welcome your support!

How can you help? Alumni can support the Millennium Scholars in a variety of ways. Do you work in a STEM field? Perhaps you could invite the Scholars to visit your business, research center, or university. Would you be interested in talking with Scholars about your research or career path, or assisting with Interview Weekend? To learn how you can support the program, please contact us: millennium@psu.edu

The Parent Association

The parents of Millennium Scholars are vital to the program's success. We expect and encourage parent engagement from Interview Weekend until graduation. The Millennium Scholars Parent Association enables parents to engage with each other and support the program. our-history.title: Our History
our-history.html:
To cultivate a community of STEM scholars who will produce sustainable solutions to global challenges and actively engage as thought leaders in society

Penn State’s first class of Millennium Scholars graduated in May 2017. To date, the Millennium Scholars Program has served over 300 scholars. At least twenty alumni have already earned advanced degrees. More than 50% of MSP alums pursue graduate education. The program currently serves 125 scholars.

Scholar's Declaration of Excellence

Excellence requires sacrifice and commitment. It is the direct result of the chances, choices, and changes that we have made. Excellence can only be achieved through the development of good habits, consistent hard work, and resilience in the face of challenges. We move forward with unwavering focus on the goal and clarity in mission.

We are determined to sacrifice now and live the rest of our lives like champions.
